articles.title: WhatsApp extortion in Calgary: Woman gets threats, then gunman fires at her home; 3 charged
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Calgary police have charged two adults and a 17-year-old boy in connection with an extortion case in which a woman was allegedly threatened through Wh.
articles.body: Calgary police have charged two adults and a 17-year-old boy in connection with an extortion case in which a woman was allegedly threatened through WhatsApp before a gun was fired at her home.The Calgary Police Service said the investigation began on March 25, when the woman started receiving unsolicited WhatsApp text and voice messages from an unknown sender demanding money.According to police, the people behind the messages appeared to have detailed knowledge of the woman's personal and business affairs. They knew her full name, home address, business information and details about her family members.The caller repeatedly tried to contact the woman and made explicit threats of violence, police said.About 12 hours after the messages were sent, an unidentified person fired a gun at the woman's residence before fleeing in a vehicle.Police did not report any injuries in the shooting.Investigators then began collecting physical and digital evidence, including security-camera footage from the area. The investigation helped police identify a vehicle believed to have been involved as well as several possible suspects.A 17-year-old boy was arrested on July 29 over his alleged role in facilitating communication between the victim and the people making the threats. He was charged with one count of extortion and has since been released from custody.The boy cannot be identified because of provisions under Canada's Youth Criminal Justice Act.As the investigation continued, police arrested a woman in Chestermere, Alberta, on September 8.Police alleged the woman provided personal information about the victim that helped the other suspects identify, locate and intimidate the woman and her family.The woman, identified as Kanureet Kaur, 23, of Chestermere, has been charged with one count of extortion. She has been released from custody and is scheduled to appear in court on October 6.Police are also looking for another suspect, Tanveer Singh, 21, of Calgary, in connection with the case.Singh is wanted on a warrant for possession of stolen property over $5,000. Police say the warrant relates to a stolen vehicle allegedly used during the shooting.Singh is described as about 5 feet 8 inches tall and weighing approximately 130 pounds. He has black hair and brown eyes.Police have released information about Singh as they seek help from the public in locating him.Calgary police also released photographs of Kaur and Singh as part of efforts to advance other extortion-related investigations.Investigators believed people involved in these cases may be known in the community by different names. Police also said members of the public may have encountered the suspects in other circumstances without knowing their identities.“While these charges are an important step, this investigation is far from over,” said Supt Jeff Bell of the Calgary Police Service's Criminal Operations and Intelligence Division.“We continue to ask the public to help us identify everyone involved so we can hold offenders accountable for the fear and harm these crimes have caused,” Bell said.The latest case is part of a wider series of extortion incidents that Calgary police have been investigating, many of which have involved members of the city's South Asian community. Police said there have been 51 extortion-related incidents in Calgary since April 2025.Of those, 19 shootings have been linked to the series, involving both people targeted by extortion and suspects, according to police.Calgary police continue to gather information about extortion attempts and related incidents across the city.Police have urged anyone who has information about the latest case, the suspects or other extortion incidents to contact investigators. Information can also be provided anonymously through Crime Stoppers. Police have also issued a warning to people who receive extortion demands: Do not pay and do not comply with the demands. articles.title: Intel chief warns of 'evolving' threats as terror groups now 'recruit their agents online'
articles.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns terrorists now recruit online, citing an alleged ISIS bomb plot near New York City's Gracie Mansion.
articles.body: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned about the growing threat global terror organizations pose to the United States through their ability to radicalize individuals online at home. Speaking on "Special Report," Clayton pointed to an attempted bombing in New York City as an example of how modern extremists no longer need distant foreign training camps to launch attacks and instead can be recruited online. Clayton responded after host Bret Baier cited United Nations figures showing that al Qaeda's global network has grown to an estimated 25,000 potential fighters — roughly 50 times its estimated size at the time of the Sept. 11 terror attacks in 2001. TOP HOUSE CHAIRMAN WARNS CONGRESS AGAINST 'COMPLACENCY' 25 YEARS AFTER 9/11 "Those numbers may be surprising. I think it's important for America to hear those numbers, but they reflect the evolving threat environment, the threat environment from terrorists," Clayton told Baier. "Terrorists recruit today much differently than they did 25 years ago," he said. AMERICAN 'JIHAD' FUELED BY 'RISKY SOURCE' INSIDE US BORDERS, WARNS NATIONAL SECURITY EXPERT Clayton said terrorists were previously often recruited and trained in camps overseas, but that process has changed in the 25 years since 9/11. "Today, they recruit their agents online. They attempt to radicalize them online," Clayton said. KASH PATEL REVEALS THE CHILLING HOLIDAY TERROR PLOTS FBI FEDERAL AGENTS QUIETLY STOPPED "Just this year, we had two radicalized men from Pennsylvania travel to New York to try and detonate a bomb outside Gracie Mansion. Thanks to the NYPD, who just like in 9/11 ran to the fire, no one was killed," he added. Federal prosecutors described both men as supporters of ISIS who consumed radical content online. Prosecutors allege the men traveled from Pennsylvania to Manhattan on March 7 with two explosive devices and attempted to detonate them near protesters and police officers outside Gracie Mansion, the official residence of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. articles.title: ‘Northern Ireland is part of UK’: Nigel Farage rejects Trump’s call for united Ireland
articles.summary: UK News: US President Donald Trump’s remarks backing a united Ireland have drawn a sharp response from Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, who said he disagreed wit.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump’s remarks backing a united Ireland have drawn a sharp response from Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, who said he disagreed with the US President and insisted that Northern Ireland is an “integral part” of the United Kingdom.Trump, speaking alongside Irish premier Micheál Martin at Farmleigh House in Dublin during his two-day visit to Ireland, said he would “love to see” Ireland unified and suggested that it was likely to happen eventually.“I don’t want to cause any problems. I have friends on both sides, great people,” Trump said when asked about Irish unity. “It’s going to happen eventually. You know what? The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. It may as well happen now.”Farage hits back at TrumpFarage, who has generally been a strong supporter of Trump, publicly disagreed with the US President over the issue.“Northern Ireland is a proud and integral part of the United Kingdom. The people of Northern Ireland neither want a referendum nor unification. I disagree with President Trump,” Farage wrote on X.His comments came as other UK politicians also criticised Trump’s remarks and stressed their support for Northern Ireland remaining part of the UK.Trump’s Ireland remarks spark UK reactionConservative leader Kemi Badenoch called Trump’s comments “deeply unhelpful”, saying that such remarks about the future of democratic countries created “unnecessary tension”.“Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom,” Badenoch said, adding that the Conservative Party would “always defend the union”.Shadow Northern Ireland secretary Alex Burghart also rejected Trump’s position, saying the US President was “very wrong” and that Northern Ireland was an “integral part” of the UK.DUP leader Gavin Robinson said Northern Ireland remained part of the UK because that was the “settled democratic will” of its people.“I am confident NI will continue to choose the UK and the security it offers,” Robinson said.Restore Britain leader Rupert Lowe, another supporter of Trump, also criticised the US President’s comments.“The American President is talking about breaking up our country. This is unacceptable, this is insulting. I like Trump, I’ve backed Trump,” Lowe said.He urged Trump not to allow his opposition to the current Labour government to damage the UK-US relationship.SDLP leader Claire Hanna took a more mocking tone, saying she suspected the DUP was “burning those Trump flags” following his remarks.Trump’s comments came during his visit to Ireland, where he also met Irish President Catherine Connolly.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Charley Hull, Lottie Woad made the wrong kind of history at the 2026 Solheim Cup
articles.summary: It has been a rough week for Team Europe's two highest-ranked players at the Solheim Cup.
articles.body:
CROMVOIRT, Netherlands — Anna Nordqvist hitched her wagon to Charley Hull and Lottie Woad and refused to change course at the 2026 Solheim Cup . Not after the English pair managed only a half point after two sessions on Friday. Nor after they suffered a 6-and-5 thrashing on Saturday morning.

By the time Nordqvist sent them out for an unprecedented fourth time on Saturday afternoon at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, the success of her captaincy might hinge on the result. The Swede was going to live and die by this top-10 pairing, and she must have figured, what are the odds they can't win one of four?

This time it was Yealimi Noh and Andrea Lee who defeated what was thought to be Europe's marquee pairing, 1 up. Noh poured in six birdies in the first nine holes to build a lead the two Englishwomen couldn't overcome.

"I don't think anyone would have beaten who we played this morning," added Woad, speaking of Lauren Coughlin and Alison Lee. "They were 7 under through 14. So credit to them, everyone's played amazing when we've played them."

The fact that Europe enters last day of the 20th edition of the Solheim Cup tied 8-8 with Hull and Woad managing only a half-point between them is a testament to the grit of a couple of rookies ― Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud ― and the inspired play of Swedes Maja Stark and Linn Grant, who put together a highlight reel of heroics to win three matches in two different formats.

Solheim Cup 2026: Best images of U.S. vs. Europe at Bernardus Golf

After Europe took a two-point lead into Saturday afternoon four-balls, Stark holed out for eagle on the first hole of the first match to send a packed crowd into a frenzy.

Stark's emphatic birdie on the 17th ended the match, 2 and 1, and put Europe's first point on the board in the afternoon. The loss ended two significant streaks for the Americans: Khang's win streak capped at six; and Coughlin suffered her first loss in the Solheim Cup in her eighth career match.

Meanwhile, the last match on the course looked almost certain to go Europe's way until Jennifer Kupcho poured in a winding putt from off the green that Dame Laura Davies' pegged at 91 feet from her perch in the commentator's box.

U.S. captain Angela Stanford took off running behind Nordqvist, who could only crack a wry smile of disbelief. Both Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier missed much shorter birdie looks to tie the hole. Then on the 18th, Kupcho drained a second birdie putt from 25 feet to bring win the last match on the course and bring the standings back to an overall tie.

Europe needs 6.5 points to win the cup while the U.S., as defending champions, needs only 6 points to retain.

Though the U.S. team has traditionally held a strong advantage in singles play, that hasn't been the case in recent years. Europe won the singles session in 2019 and 2024, and the two teams tied in 2017, 2021, 2023. The U.S. team has won on foreign soil only three times, the most recent coming in 2015.

Coming in, both teams were strong at the top of their lineups but thin down low. That's probably why Nordqvist decided from the start that Hull and Woad would both play all five matches. That they would play all four paired matches together, Woad said, was always Plan A.

Randy Robles of Elias Sports Bureau has been cranking out stats all week for the media, and he uncovered an unfortunate new record for this pair: In the history of the Solheim Cup, there have been 43 instances of players competing in all four matches prior to singles. Woad and Hull are the only ones who have earned less than a full point. in total.

Woad, the rookie, isn't hanging her head about it.

"Doesn't matter who wins the points," she said of the team's position. "I would happily lose my matches if we win."

Beth Ann Nichols is a senior writer for Golfweek covering the LPGA and all things women's golf. Follow her on X/Twitter (@GolfweekNichols).
